western.temperament: Disciplined, patient, reliable, takes charge, stays the course; shadow: a hard protective shell, slow to share feelings, can read as cold, can over-focus on success.
western.modality: Cardinal; negative polarity; opposite sign Cancer

chinese.temperament: Loyal, honest, kind, cautious, protective, reliable; goes to great lengths for its few important people. Shadow: reserved at first, avoids the spotlight, struggles to voice thoughts so can seem stubborn.

symbolism.meaning: The bear sits under the yeti legend. Swami Pranavananda derived the 'teh/ti' in yeti from Tibetan dred (spoken 'tre'), bear; Dzu-teh is glossed 'cattle bear'. Messner concluded the yeti is a bear. Two scraps of 'yeti fur' from Hillary's 1960 expedition were identified as blue bear pelt. Lindqvist et al. 2017 (Proc. R. Soc. B) found a femur from a 'yeti' in a Tibetan Plateau cave and a 1950s Nepal hair sample were Tibetan brown bear. The bear is the real animal behind a legend people preferred to the animal.

symbolism.culture: Tibetan Buddhism (yeti, via the same lore)
symbolism.meaning: The yeti was adopted into Tibetan Buddhism as a nonhuman animal that can sometimes follow the Dharma; Bön held the blood of the mi rgod ('wild man') useful in ceremonies. This is yeti belief, not bear belief: use only as context for item 1, never as 'bear medicine'.

symbolism.culture: Chinese, Shijing (Book of Songs), ode Si Gan 斯干 Sī Gān
symbolism.meaning: A lucky dream of bears, 維熊維羆 wéi xióng wéi pí ('bears and grizzly bears'), is read by the diviner as 男子之祥 nánzǐ zhī xiáng, an omen of a son. Generic bears, not this subspecies: a bear in a dream as strength arriving.

In Chinese it is 藏馬熊 zàng mǎxióng (simplified 藏马熊), the Tibetan horse bear, or 西藏棕熊 Xīzàng zōngxióng; English sources also list 'horse bear'. Our reading: a Dog-year animal carrying the Horse in its name, and the Horse is in the Dog's trine.

Long known in the West only from a few furs and bones; 'one of the rarest subspecies of bear in the world, rarely sighted in the wild'. First documented evidence in India came from North Sikkim above 4,000 m in 2024.
'Blue bear spirit animal' or 'blue bear totem' meanings: none found in any traditional source. The coat is not blue (see audit).

fusion.temperament: Our reading: doubled Earth with no counterweight. Saturn's schedule meets the Dog's guard post. The bear holds high, poor ground where food is far apart, so it spends little and wastes nothing. Steady, watchful, hard to find, completely there once found.
fusion.gifts: Our reading: endurance on thin rations, loyalty that does not need an audience, judgment about who has earned access, calm in exposed places, and the ability to finish what others abandon at the treeline.
fusion.shadow: Our reading: the legend gets bigger than the bear. Letting rumour stand in for contact, staying unconfirmed by the people who would welcome you, Capricorn's hard shell plus the Dog's reluctance to speak until the silence itself becomes the answer.
fusion.love: Our reading: slow to let anyone close, then fiercely protective. The pale collar runs from shoulder to chest and only shows when the bear turns to face you; love here means turning to face someone on purpose. Best with partners who are patient climbers and do not demand proof of feeling on a timetable.
fusion.money: Our reading: Saturn and Earth make a careful saver who budgets like the plateau: few meals, planned far apart. The risk is hoarding past need and refusing help that would cost nothing.
fusion.conflict: Our reading: climbs away and goes quiet rather than argues; returns only when the ground feels safe. Rarely starts a fight, defends its few people hard. The Dragon-year types who storm in loudly are the hardest for it.

careers.path: Field research, rangers, conservation in remote places
careers.why: Our reading: comfortable far from crowds and on hard terrain; Capricorn persistence.
Our reading: the Dog's guard instinct plus Saturn's rules; spots the weak point on the route first.

careers.path: Engineering, surveying, mountain or infrastructure work
careers.why: Our reading: doubled Earth; structures that must hold weight for decades.
Our reading: a subspecies known for decades from a few furs and bones; patience with thin evidence.
Our reading: works best with judgment trusted and no daily performance of effort.

candidate_lines: Above four thousand metres the grass is thin and the walk between meals is long, and you were built for that arithmetic: little given, little asked, nothing wasted.
Half the stories told about you on the plateau were really about a wild man in the snow, and you let them run, because a rumour keeps strangers further down the slope than any fence.
The pale collar only shows when you rise and turn toward someone. Few have seen it, and every one of them climbed a long way first.
Saturn gave you the schedule and the Dog gave you the post, and some winters you hold both so long the valley stops expecting you back.
Your word, once given, behaves like a den dug into scree: hard to find, harder to dig out, still there when April comes.
On the plateau they call you horse bear, and it fits: the friend who finally coaxes you off the ridge is usually a runner, rarely a reasoner.

fact_audit.fact: Header hanzi 熊 (rail__han and serial-han), pinyin xióng
fact_audit.note: 熊 xióng means 'bear' in general. Not wrong, but it does not name this animal. Specific traditional name: 藏馬熊 zàng mǎxióng (Tibetan horse bear); alternative 西藏棕熊 Xīzàng zōngxióng (Tibetan brown bear). Recommend 藏馬熊 if the rail allows three glyphs, otherwise keep 熊.

fact_audit.fact: Intro: 'dark blue-grey in coat with a pale patch at the throat'
fact_audit.note: Coat ranges from dark brown to creamy white, with lighter areas on head, neck and back in some individuals (s12); the distinctive mark is a 'yellowish scarf-like collar that broadens from the shoulders to the chest' (s11), not a throat patch. 'Blue' is an old Western name, not the coat colour. Also fixes the page's recurring 'pale mark at your throat' imagery: say collar across shoulders and chest.

fact_audit.fact: Fact 1: a recent species-wide review of brown bear subspecies by the IBA names grizzly, Kodiak and tentative Gobi, and does not list the Tibetan population
fact_audit.note: The IBA brown bear species profile names U. a. horribilis, U. a. middendorffi, northwest Eurasian U. a. arctos and a tentative Gobi population, and does not mention pruinosus (s13). But it is a species web profile, not a 'review of subspecies'. And U. a. pruinosus (Blyth 1854) is a named, widely used subspecies (s6). Rewrite as 'the IBA's brown bear profile does not mention it'.

fact_audit.fact: Fact 2: brown bears range from sea level to about 5,000 m; Tibetan population at the uppermost edge, alpine meadows and scree above treeline
fact_audit.note: IBA: 'any altitude between sea level and 5,000 m' (s13). Tibetan brown bear habitat: alpine forests, meadows and steppe above 4,000 m (s11).

fact_audit.fact: Fact 3: excellent smell over long distances, human-level hearing, comparatively poor eyesight
fact_audit.note: ADW: excellent smell (carcass scent over two miles), human-level hearing, 'relatively poor eyesight' (s14). These are Ursus arctos generalities, not Tibetan-specific findings; say 'brown bears'. Bear eyesight being poor is contested in popular sources; keep 'relatively'.

fact_audit.fact: Fact 4: winter dormancy lowers heart rate and metabolism, not true deep torpor, can be roused readily
fact_audit.note: IBA: no deep torpor bouts typical of rodents; easily active if disturbed (s13). ADW: 'not true hibernation', 'aroused readily' (s14). Species-level, not studied in the Tibetan population.

fact_audit.fact: Fact 5: largely solitary outside mating and mother-cub groups; overlapping home ranges
fact_audit.note: ADW: generally solitary, only female-young bonds; home ranges overlap extensively, no territorial defence (s14). Species-level.

fact_audit.fact: Fact 6: gall bladders sold on traditional medicine markets with no documented benefit; illegal trade a threat across the range, Tibetan Plateau included
fact_audit.note: ADW supports the gall bladder trade and the lack of documented medicinal value (s14); IBA lists illegal trade in bear parts (s13). For the Tibetan population specifically, Wikipedia's bile-threat sentence carries 'citation needed' (s6). Drop 'the Tibetan Plateau included' or source it.

fact_audit.fact: Hero: rarely photographed, real sightings still notable events
fact_audit.note: 'One of the rarest subspecies of bear in the world... rarely sighted in the wild' (s6, s11).

fact_audit.fact: Crossing: January or early February birthdays can belong to the Rooster; Dog years 1994, 2006, 2018
fact_audit.note: Applies to Capricorn (late Dec to 20 Jan). Rooster precedes Dog. 2018 Dog year ran 16 Feb 2018 to 4 Feb 2019 (s4).

fact_audit.fact: Proverb 犬馬之勞 quǎn mǎ zhī láo, labelled as our own pairing
fact_audit.note: Real idiom; the page honestly labels the pairing as its own. Note it also carries the Horse, the Dog's trine partner.
